text:
Diego Morales: Hi team  got the vendor migration notice for our 401(k) and HSA on Friday. Two quick questions: 1) I have an outstanding 401(k) loan  will that transfer cleanly to the new vendor? 2) My HSA debit card is used for recurring prescriptions  will card transactions be blocked during the blackout? Any employee action required?

Claire Nguyen: Good questions. Short answers: loans generally transfer to the new recordkeeper and payroll loan withholdings should continue, but theres often a short blackout window. HSA card activity can be interrupted while account numbers are migrated.

Terry (Benefits Ops): Adding specifics from the migration checklist we sent:
- 401(k) loans: plan loan records will move; payroll withholding for loan repayment continues as usual in most cases. If payroll sees a mismatch during cutover we may suspend withholding for 1-2 pay cycles. If you notice withholdings stop >1 pay cycle, file a payroll ticket immediately so we can request an urgent fix.
- Loan default risk: if loan repayments stop and remain unpaid for >90 days OR the loan goes into default per plan rules, the loan could be treated as a taxable distribution. We will proactively monitor and notify anyone affected.
- HSA debit cards: transactions can decline during the vendor blackout. The vendor usually issues new cards after conversion; old cards may be automatically reissued, but merchant-specific tokenization (e.g., stored cards at pharmacies) might need reauthorization.

Terry (Benefits Ops): Employee action items: 1) If you have autopay or recurring charges tied to your HSA card, consider adding a backup payment method with your provider for the blackout week. 2) Print or save any statements you might need for reimbursement during the migration window. 3) Check your mailbox for the new card mailing address; if it's wrong, update with benefits@redwood.com immediately.

Diego Morales: Thanks. What about rollovers or in-service distributions I submitted last week? Will those be processed or delayed?

Terry (Benefits Ops): In-service distributions and pending rollovers submitted before the blackout will be processed as long as they were fully approved and in flight before the cutoff timestamp the vendor communicated. Anything submitted during the blackout will be queued and processed after migration completes. We advised employees to avoid initiating time-sensitive transactions within 72 hours of the cutoff.

Claire Nguyen: Also note: your vesting schedule and historical employer match records do not reset because of a vendor change. The plan sponsor (Redwood) maintains plan terms and vesting rules. A recordkeeper change only moves the administration of those records. If the plan itself is amended (different match formula), that affects future contributions only as of the amendment effective date.

Diego Morales: Good to hear vesting history stays intact. One more: will loans be repayable via ACH if payroll issues occur?

Terry (Benefits Ops): Some participants have used ACH to the recordkeeper in exceptional cases, but that requires plan admin approval and manual reconciliation. If payroll withholding is interrupted, we will contact affected employees to offer temporary ACH options only when necessary. Reach out to benefits@redwood.com if you want to pre-authorize contingency ACH instructions.

PayrollBot: Automated notice: "Payroll system will attempt normal loan withholding during conversion. If a stop is detected, payroll@redwood.com will create a case and notify the employee. Do not manually attempt to withhold or adjust pre-tax deferrals without HR guidance"

hr-bot: Policy snippet (automated): "Vendor transitions may cause short service disruptions. Plan terms, vesting schedules, and participant balances remain subject to the plan document. Employees are responsible for monitoring paychecks and reporting any withholding interruptions within 2 pay cycles."

Diego Morales: Great, thanks everyone. Ill monitor my card and paychecks and open a payroll ticket if I see issues. Appreciate the clear steps.

Terry (Benefits Ops): Well post a migration status thread in #people-ops and send email updates. Tag us if you run into anything.

Claire Nguyen: FYI we uploaded an FAQ doc to the benefits portal with screenshots of expected emails/cards. Link in the migration announcement.

Diego Morales: Perfect. Thanks!
